ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum determinism is: every trusted derivation is a total mathematical function of its committed input closure — byte-identical output on every re-execution within the pinned hardware/software class declared in the closure — where the closure explicitly includes every reified nondeterminism source (logical clock value, seeds, parallel merge schedule, canonical orderings, pinned toolchain identity). UNTRUSTED PRODUCERS ARE DETERMINIZABLE PER PINNED CLASS (v1 exclusion retracted): pinned model weights plus batch-invariant inference kernels yield bit-identical candidate generation as a pure function of the committed closure within a pinned hardware/driver class, so where deployed, producer outputs enter the committed closure as replayable derivations rather than opaque captures; the irreducible residue is CROSS-HARDWARE bit-portability, handled by record/replay of the committed candidate bytes. Nondeterminism that remains outside the trusted path (unpinned producers, network fetches) crosses into it solely as committed bytes. Byte-identity is the terminal point: no stronger equivalence than bit equality exists. The one true exclusion: determinism against hardware faults (bit flips) — attainable form is detection by AX-13 verification, not prevention.
derivation: A computation's output depends only on its inputs; determinism is maximal exactly when the input set is closed — every read of wall-clock, RNG, scheduler order, iteration order, or filesystem enumeration is banished or committed. Nothing exceeds output = f(committed closure); any residual dependence on an uncommitted quantity is nondeterminism by definition. Byte-identity across machines requires the implementation semantics in the closure (pinned runtime version, IEEE-754 behavior) — a closure item, not a weakening. The v1 claim that determinizing untrusted producers is impossible is retracted on the corpus's own evidence class: batch-invariant kernels deliver bit-identical model outputs under frozen inputs (at a throughput cost), so substrate-level determinism of statistical producers is achievable per pinned hardware/software class; H1 still bars their outputs from the trusted path as JUDGMENTS, but their GENERATION becomes a replayable derivation, strictly enlarging the replayable perimeter. The honest residue is cross-hardware portability: bit-identity across differing accelerator/driver classes is not guaranteed, and the ceiling handles it by committing the produced bytes (record/replay). This does not weaken the ABSOLUTE core — output = f(closure) — it extends its reach.
ceiling_kind: ABSOLUTE (output = f(committed closure) core; per-pinned-class scope for producer determinization stated inside the closure semantics)
lean_obligation: Theorem (deterministic step + confluent join): (1) the trusted small-step relation is a function: Step s a and Step s b imply a = b, with the state including the committed closure and no other environment; (2) parallel schedule irrelevance: any two DAG-admitted interleavings yield equal results (diamond/commutation via Newman's lemma on the finite DAG); corollary: run : Closure -> Output is a function, making nondeterminism unrepresentable; (3) producer-determinization scope: model a pinned producer as gen : Closure -> Bytes total within a declared class C; prove replay equality within C and NO claim across classes — the cross-hardware residue appears as an explicit class index in the theorem statement, so the limit of the determinization claim is syntactically visible.
